$comment: IGNORED BY THE LOADER. External sources of React components, at LIBRARY granularity and BY REFERENCE ONLY. No third party's component source is stored here, and no `files`/`content` field exists in this schema to store it in. Each entry carries what you need to CHOOSE a source and to know what you may do with it: a name, a URL, a licence, and what it is for. Every licence below was verified on 2026-07-29 by reading the project's own LICENSE file or licence page; the URLs are in the provenance blocks and the evidence is in docs/GUI_CATALOGUE.md. Three of these are licence traps -- read `use_mode` before copying anything.

entries.name: ext/shadcn-ui
entries.title: shadcn/ui
entries.purpose: The reference copy-in component collection for React and Tailwind: accordion, button, dialog, form, table and about sixty more primitives you paste into your own repo and then own. Also the publisher of registry.json / registry-item.json, the only widely-adopted machine-readable schema for describing available components. Reach for this first when you need a conventional, accessible, unopinionated widget.

provenance.note: LICENSE.md read raw: 'MIT License / Copyright (c) 2023 shadcn'. One repo-root licence covers docs, CLI and the component source served in files[].content. Registry index https://ui.shadcn.com/r/index.json fetched: HTTP 200, no auth, 62 registry:ui items, metadata only, no source.

entries.usage: npx shadcn@latest add button    # copies source into YOUR repo; nothing is vendored here
entries.notes: The FORMAT this catalogue's schema is modelled on. Two things its registry-item schema provably lacks, verified by fetching https://ui.shadcn.com/schema/registry-item.json: no props/API field anywhere (only a meta.links.*.api URL to somebody's prose docs), and no licence or provenance field at all. Both are mandatory here. Per-item URLs (/r/styles/<style>/<name>.json) DO embed full component source in files[].content -- fetching those is how you would accidentally vendor.

entries.name: ext/react-bits
entries.title: React Bits
entries.purpose: A large collection of animated, eye-catching React components -- text effects, backgrounds, scroll and hover animations. Visually the closest match to a 'wow' brief. USE IT AS INSPIRATION AND REFERENCE ONLY: its licence forbids redistributing the components, so its source may not be copied into a repository that is itself redistributed.

provenance.note: LICENSE.md read raw: 'MIT + Commons Clause License Condition v1.0 -- Copyright (c) 2026 David Haz ... so long as you do not sell, sublicense, or redistribute the components themselves -- whether alone, in a bundle, or as a ported version.' GitHub's own detector reports key 'other', spdx 'NOASSERTION'.

entries.notes: THE LICENCE TRAP THIS CATALOGUE EXISTS TO CATCH. The string starts with 'MIT'; the licence is not MIT. The Commons Clause removes exactly the right this repo would need. There is no official registry.json and no official MCP server -- the MCP servers on npm are third-party wrappers, unaffiliated with the author. Separately: the npm package literally named `react-bits` is an UNRELATED project by Doug Miller and is not this.

entries.name: ext/aceternity-ui
entries.title: Aceternity UI
entries.purpose: Elaborate motion-heavy React and Tailwind components -- 3D cards, spotlight and aurora backgrounds, animated beams. Serves a similar brief to React Bits with a heavier framer-motion dependency. Reference only: the licence permits building and selling end products but forbids redistributing the source files.

provenance.note: Licence page read: custom 'Aceternity License' -- permits building and selling end-products, prohibits 're-distributing the Item or source files' and selling derivative products on marketplaces. Live shadcn-format registry confirmed at https://ui.aceternity.com/registry/<name>.json (returns full .tsx source, no auth). Whether paid components are gated in the same registry was NOT confirmed.

entries.notes: Serves a live shadcn-format registry that embeds source and needs no auth. Being fetchable is not being licensed: the registry works, the licence still forbids redistribution. Do not let the CLI's success be read as permission.

entries.name: ext/magic-ui
entries.title: Magic UI
entries.purpose: Around 150 animated copy-in components in the shadcn registry format -- marquees, shimmer buttons, number tickers, animated beams and grids. MIT, so unlike React Bits and Aceternity its source genuinely may be copied. Reach for it when a landing page or a marketing surface needs motion the glass set does not cover.

provenance.note: LICENSE.md confirmed MIT. registry.json present at repo root (HTTP 200 on raw.githubusercontent.com) and listed in shadcn's registry directory as @magicui -> https://magicui.design/r/{name}.

entries.notes: Copy-in, not npm-installable. Individual components commonly require `motion` (framer-motion); the per-component dependency list was NOT verified entry by entry.

entries.name: ext/radix-primitives
entries.title: Radix UI Primitives
entries.purpose: Unstyled, accessible behaviour primitives: dialog, popover, dropdown menu, tooltip, select, tabs. It supplies focus trapping, keyboard interaction, ARIA wiring and collision-aware positioning -- the hard parts the glass set deliberately does not implement. Reach for it when a glass component needs real modal or menu semantics rather than a styled div.

provenance.note: LICENSE read raw from the repo: MIT.

entries.notes: A REAL npm RUNTIME DEPENDENCY, not copy-in -- the one entry here that would add packages to apps/web/package.json. Relevant because glass/GlassSheet sets role="dialog" and aria-modal but does NOT trap focus; Radix Dialog is the standard way to close that gap. Adding it is a dependency decision for a human, not something a build skill may take on its own.

entries.name: ext/base-ui
entries.title: Base UI
entries.purpose: Unstyled accessible React primitives from the MUI and Floating UI authors; the same brief as Radix and increasingly what shadcn/ui's own components link to for API documentation. An alternative headless layer when Radix is not preferred.
entries.notes: npm runtime dependency. shadcn/ui's registry index links Base UI docs from meta.links.base.api for several components.

entries.name: ext/headless-ui
entries.title: Headless UI
entries.purpose: Tailwind Labs' unstyled accessible components: menu, listbox, combobox, dialog, disclosure, transitions. Smaller surface than Radix, and the natural pairing if a project is already all-in on Tailwind.

entries.name: ext/ark-ui
entries.title: Ark UI
entries.purpose: Headless, state-machine-driven components (Zag.js underneath) for React, Vue and Solid. Reach for it when a component's interaction is genuinely stateful -- a multi-step date picker, a complex combobox -- and an explicit state machine is worth the weight.
entries.notes: npm runtime dependency. Park UI is the styled layer built on top of it.

entries.name: ext/tremor
entries.title: Tremor
entries.purpose: React components for dashboards and analytics: charts, KPI cards, bar lists, spark charts, data tables. The obvious source when a built GUI needs real data visualisation, which the glass set does not cover at all.

provenance.note: LICENSE read raw: Apache-2.0, with named subcomponents noted as MIT-adapted from Radix, shadcn and Medusa. The Jan-2025 Vercel acquisition changed pricing/access for paid templates, NOT the code licence.

entries.notes: Two distributions: `@tremor/react` (npm dependency) and 'Tremor Raw' (copy-in). Apache-2.0 requires the notice be preserved -- which this repo is already set up for, being Apache-2.0 itself.

entries.name: ext/origin-ui
entries.title: Origin UI
entries.purpose: A large collection of copy-in Tailwind and React components, heavy on form inputs and field variations. Useful as reference for input patterns. CHECK THE LICENCE PER DIRECTORY before copying anything -- the repository default is AGPL-3.0.

provenance.note: Repository default licence is AGPL-3.0 (full text read raw). LICENSING.md carves out apps/origin/ and apps/ui/ as MIT. Recorded here at the REPOSITORY DEFAULT -- the conservative reading -- because a per-directory carve-out is a per-file question a table lookup must not answer.

entries.notes: SPLIT LICENCE. Recorded as AGPL-3.0 so use_mode comes out 'reciprocal' and a human is forced to look. The MIT carve-out is real but is scoped to two directories; resolving which files it covers is not a decision this catalogue may make.

entries.name: ext/21st-dev
entries.title: 21st.dev
entries.purpose: A marketplace and registry aggregating community-published shadcn-compatible components, with a search API and an MCP server for retrieving component code. Useful for DISCOVERY -- finding that a pattern exists and who published it. Not a source you may copy from without checking each component's own terms.

provenance.note: Terms read: component 'code, content, and materials ... are the sole and exclusive property of their respective authors and 21st Labs Inc', with uncredited redistribution prohibited. The PLATFORM repos (serafimcloud/21st, 21st-dev/registry) are MIT -- that covers the tooling, not the marketplace content.

entries.notes: The MIT badge on the platform repository does NOT license the components. This is the second shape of the same trap as React Bits: a permissive licence attached to a neighbouring artifact. Per-component terms must be checked individually.

entries.name: ext/motion-primitives
entries.title: Motion Primitives
entries.purpose: Copy-in animated React components and motion patterns built on framer-motion -- text effects, transitions, disclosure animations. Closest external match to this repo's own motion vocabulary, and MIT, so its patterns may genuinely be adapted.

provenance.note: MIT. Listed in shadcn's registry directory; items served at /c/{name}.json.

entries.notes: Requires `motion` (framer-motion), which apps/web already depends on.

entries.name: ext/mui
entries.title: MUI (Material UI)
entries.purpose: The large, mature Material Design component kit for React: full widget coverage, theming, data grid, date pickers. Reach for it only when a project wants Material Design as its identity -- it is stylistically the opposite of the glass set and will not blend with it.

provenance.note: @mui/material core is MIT. MUI X Pro/Premium packages (@mui/x-data-grid-pro and siblings) ship a separate 'Commercial License / Copyright (c) 2020 Material-UI SAS' file and are governed by the EULA at https://mui.com/legal/mui-x-eula.

entries.notes: MIXED LICENSING WITHIN ONE BRAND. The MIT here covers the CORE only. MUI X Pro and Premium are commercial and are NOT covered by this entry; treat any @mui/x-*-pro or -premium package as a separate, paid decision.

entries.name: ext/mantine
entries.title: Mantine
entries.purpose: A broad MIT component and hooks library for React with strong form handling, notifications, modals and a large hooks collection. A conventional npm alternative to assembling primitives by hand.

entries.name: ext/skiper-ui
entries.title: Skiper UI
entries.purpose: Copy-in animated shadcn-compatible components. Listed in shadcn's registry directory. ITS LICENCE COULD NOT BE ESTABLISHED, so nothing may be copied from it until a human reads one.

provenance.note: No LICENSE file was located for the canonical repository on 2026-07-29. Recorded as NOASSERTION -- an explicit 'we looked and could not establish it', which is a finding, not an absence.

entries.notes: PRESENT DELIBERATELY, as the worked example of the honest third state. A missing licence FIELD is a refusal -- such an entry never loads. An explicitly recorded NOASSERTION loads and resolves to reference_only, so the library stays discoverable while its source stays uncopyable. Reopen when someone reads a licence.
